Subject: Orchid Health discovery — integration walkthrough & action items

Hi Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the suggested next steps so we have a shared record. Please reply with any corrections.

What we heard (pain points)
- Current triage pipeline has 600–900ms median latency on lookup + ranking, causing clinician friction during intake.
- Several downstream systems require structured outputs (JSON with standardized fields) for EHR ingestion.
- Relevance of retrieval+rerank varies by specialty; need per-department tuning and an easy A/B testing surface.

Goals you articulated
- Reduce end-to-end patient-intake latency to <300ms for short prompts/embeds path.
- Deploy a PoC that demonstrates embedding + rerank improvements for triage suggestions and captures structured form outputs for 4 high-volume workflows.
- Keep PHI in a private deployment (VPC) or dedicated capacity; procurement will confirm later.

Integration & product fit notes
- Recommended Redwood capabilities: streaming function-calls for incremental UI updates during triage, embedding + reranker combo to improve top-K suggestions, and structured-output schemas for direct EHR patching.
- SDK changes we’ll need on our side (high level): implement streaming client hooks, pass structured-output schema in prompts, and opt-in KV/prefix caching for repeated patient-context queries.
- For security: we can run the PoC on Dedicated with customer-managed KMS; procurement asked for SOC2 evidence (we’ll pull that into the packet).

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
1) Redwood to produce a 2-week PoC plan (technical checklist + infra needs) — owner: Hannah — ETA: 2027-11-05.
2) Orchid to provide three sample anonymized workflows and one flattened dataset for preliminary embedding tests — owner: Maya — ETA: 2027-11-08.
3) Joint tech deep-dive to finalize function-call contract and structured-output schemas — owner: Jordan (Redwood) / Maya (Orchid) — scheduled: propose Nov 9.
4) Procurement kickoff to surface contract requirements and infra preferences — owner: Orchid procurement — ETA: 2027-11-10.

Attachments: I’ve attached a preliminary integration scope (orchid-integration-scope.xlsx) and an editable SOW stub (orchid-sow-draft.pdf) for procurement and legal to review.

Questions we still have
- For ranking: can you confirm typical query lengths and expected QPS during peak clinic hours?
- Is there an internal ID mapping we should use when returning structured outputs so downstream unification is trivial?

Happy to jump on a short follow-up today if you want to tighten the plan.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — this is a great summary, and yes, aligns with what we discussed. A couple of small clarifications:
- Peak QPS is closer to 40–60 for triage during morning surge windows; median prompt length for triage suggestions is ~28 tokens, but retrieval context pushes some calls to 300–400 tokens.
- We have an internal patient-event ID (event_id) we’d like returned in the structured output so our ingestion job can upsert reliably.

I’ll upload the three anonymized workflows and the flattened sample dataset to the shared Drive folder by EOD Monday (Nov 8).

Nov 9 works for the tech deep-dive — 10:30am PT would be ideal. Would Jordan be the primary on the Redwood side?

Procurement will start compiling questions against your SOW stub — they may request an on-prem option for a formal security review, but for the PoC we prefer Dedicated capacity.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the PoC plan.

Best,
